title: Add canonical run manifest JSON schema + validator; ship example manifests; add CI to prevent drift
author: Rina Kobayashi
body: Context: For the Q1'26 Perf baseline & representative workload suite we need results to be reproducible and attributable across runs, regions, GPU SKUs, and scheduler/kernel changes. Today our benchmark harnesses emit slightly different “metadata blobs”, which makes run comparison brittle and blocks automated gating. This PR introduces the canonical “run manifest” format and enforcement tooling per ADR-0172 (benchmark metrics + run manifest schema). What’s in this PR: (1) JSON Schema for the canonical run manifest (schema id + semver) covering environment capture (driver/CUDA, OS image, container digest), runtime build identifiers, model identifiers/config, scheduler config pointers, workload definition + seed, run mode (streaming/non-streaming), and required tags (region, sku, cohort). (2) A small validator CLI that can be used locally and in CI to validate manifests (and optionally “results.json” headers) against the schema. (3) Example manifests for the v1 workload shapes (chat streaming, long-prefill summarization, embeddings high-QPS) that teams can copy/paste to start running baselines. (4) CI check to prevent schema drift and to ensure any example manifests in-repo continue to validate. Design notes: The schema is intentionally strict on identity + env capture fields (to support attribution) and intentionally flexible on workload_parameters via a “workload_ref” + “params” object with a controlled allowlist (to avoid embedding sensitive prompt content). The schema includes explicit versioning (manifest_version) and supports forward-compatible additions via optional fields, but disallows unknown top-level fields to keep producers honest. Validator usage: ./tools/validate_manifest --schema schemas/run-manifest/v1/run_manifest.schema.json --manifest examples/manifests/chat_streaming_llama_70b_h100_us-east.json; CI runs this on every PR touching schemas/ or examples/. Testing: Unit tests for validator; schema tests for required/optional field behavior; golden tests for example manifests. Rollout: This is additive; existing harnesses can keep emitting old metadata while we migrate. Follow-ups (tracked in ENG-4822): wire validator into perf-canary and enforce presence of manifest for all baseline uploads; migrate legacy harnesses to emit v1 manifest sidecar.
commits: schemas: add run_manifest.schema.json (v1) with strict top-level required fields
tools: add validate_manifest CLI (python) + unit tests
examples: add v1 example manifests for representative workloads
ci: add GitHub Actions job to validate schema/examples and prevent drift
docs: add README describing manifest fields, versioning, and migration guidance
review_conversation: Claire Dubois (review): Can we make the schema enforce a stable “workload_ref” and keep raw prompt content out entirely? Also please clarify what “ttft_boundary” means (first token computed vs first token on wire).

Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated schema to require workload_ref and to disallow prompt content at top-level; also added doc text explaining that measurement boundaries belong in results headers, not the manifest. Removed ttft_boundary from manifest; added guidance to results format doc stub.
Jonas Weber (review): Please add a manifest_version field and an explicit $id so downstream tools can pin. Also would like examples to include streaming cadence and seed to support reproducibility.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added manifest_version (v1.0.0) and $id; examples now include seed, request_mix_ref, and streaming.pacing_ms where applicable.
Sean Gallagher (review): For attribution we need kernel/runtime build identifiers to be non-ambiguous. Can we require container_image_digest and runtime_git_sha (or build_id)?
Rina Kobayashi (author): Required container_image.digest and runtime.build_id. build_id supports monorepo CI build IDs and/or git sha; docs updated with examples for both.
Allison Grant (review): Please align metric tag names with observability conventions (region, sku, model, workload). Also can you add a guardrail in CI so schema changes require updating examples?

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added tagging section to README; CI now fails if examples don’t validate, and includes an additional step that checks example manifests reference the current schema path/version.
Claire Dubois (final): Approved once the README explicitly calls out unknown top-level fields are rejected (prevents silent drift).
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added “Strictness” section to README + a unit test that asserts unknown fields fail validation.
